maria: Heads-up — after the kernel selector flip at 09:12 we saw a new p99 tail for short requests. Suspect interaction between the new kernel affinity and our micro-batch alignment (microgap smoothing).

sam: can you paste the numbers + a short repro?

maria: quick snapshot from the canary (10k requests over 30m):
```
baseline (old kernel): p50=12ms p95=28ms p99=42ms throughput=12k rps kv_hit=93%
canary (new kernel + smoothing): p50=13ms p95=35ms p99=88ms throughput=11.1k rps kv_hit=67%
error rate stable, CPU on host +6%, GPU occupancy similar
```
The interesting bit: p99 jump correlates with bursts of tiny windows (microgaps) that cause single-request batches to fire, then the new kernel has slightly higher per-token setup and we lose KV warming because coalesced prefixes are split.

alex: that matches a hypothesis: smoothing reduced variance but increased the chance of buckets firing just-before KV priming completes. If a request hits an unprimed KV for long sequences, kernel selection chooses the new kernel path which has slower early-token latency.

rachel: do we have the batch size / coalesce timers around those spikes?

maria: yes — relevant config excerpt from the canary service: `micro_batch_interval_ms=2`, `coalesce_delay_ms=1`, `jitter_ms=0.6`, `token_budget_target=1024`, `queue_capacity=512`.

alex: two levers I want to try: 1) widen micro_batch_interval to 4ms to give KV priming more headroom, 2) increase jitter to 1.2ms to desynchronize pathological alignments. That should reduce single-request singleton batches. Risk: slight increase in median.

sam: alternative is to lower token_budget_target to create smaller batches but safer KV priming per batch. try `token_budget_target=800`?

maria: plan proposal — run parallel canaries:
- canary A: micro_batch_interval_ms=4, jitter_ms=1.2, token_budget_target=1024
- canary B: micro_batch_interval_ms=2, jitter_ms=0.6, token_budget_target=800
Measure p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, throughput, and kernel-selection split.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-A -> cluster-a at 09:50, canary-B -> cluster-b at 09:55 (auto-rollout disabled).

devex-bot: dashboard links: https://internal.redwood/prod/canaries/3928123456-A and /B (plots: latency by token_len, kv_hit heatmap, kernel_breakdown).

alex: also add a light fallback: if p99 for short requests > 60ms for 5m, route new-kernel traffic to fallback kernel variant that keeps old warmup path. Should avoid customer impact while we iterate.

sam: i'll own canary B and the rollback hook. alex you own fallback rule. maria monitor kv_hit heatmap and perf traces. rachel collect traces for token_len>512.

maria: acknowledged. I'll post a follow-up summary after the 30m run. Initial guess: we can recover p99 to <50ms by either increasing microgap allowance or lowering token caps.

rachel: :thumbsup: ask: include a tiny perf profile (nvprof / on-host trace) if we still see unexplained kernel setup spikes.

sam: quick command i'll run for the canary trace dump:
```
./tools/trace-collect --cluster cluster-b --since now-35m --filter "kernel=new_kernel" --out /tmp/trace-canaryB
```

maria: thanks — I'll also attach a sample request id list so we can correlate traces to exact microgap events.

alex: small note — if we go with wider micro_batch_interval, feed that config into the autoscaler policy so spike-handling doesn't collapse queue_capacity badly.

rachel: noted.

maria: OK deploying now. will report back in ~40m with numbers and a short recommendation. :rocket:
